warnings: This sheet (A-14) presents 3 door types (D1-D3, circle symbols, top row) and 5 window types (W1-W5, hexagon symbols, top-row-4th-cell + entire bottom row) — same 3-doors/5-windows split as house #03's equivalent A-13 sheet, strongly confirming the shared government-housing-program template (same door/window dimensions, materials, and even the same W5 stairwell-landing note, almost verbatim).

One genuine per-house difference from house #03's version: W1's glass here is 'กระจกใส หนา 5มม' (5mm) vs house #03's W1 at 6mm — re-verified by close crop, reads clearly as '5มม.' not '6มม.' Recorded as printed, not corrected to match the sister house.

Height-breakdown convention (re-derived this pass, applies to all 5 windows): the SUM of all segments except the last equals the drawn window-frame graphic's own height; the LAST (bottom-most) segment is always an un-drawn sill/wall gap down to floor level, never part of the frame graphic itself. Confirmed directly for W1/W2/W4 (single-panel graphic = the '1.20' segment only, '0.85' undrawn below) and for W3/W5 (multi-tier graphics = all segments but the last, undrawn sill below) via close crops taken this pass. This resolves an ambiguity flagged as unresolved on a sister house's equivalent W3 entry ('height_breakdown_order_(1.80_then_0.50_vs_reverse)_not_fully_certain').

D/W numbering re-derived by position/type since the sheet's own per-cell symbol numbering restarts independently for doors (circle 1,2,3) vs windows (hexagon 1,2,3,4,5) and would collide if used verbatim as element_id — same convention used project-wide for this sheet type.

W5 lights a stairwell at the stair-landing level, per its printed '▼ ระดับชานพักบันได' annotation directly under the elevation graphic — consistent with a stair core appearing in this house's floor plans/sections (see หน้า15's รูปตัด 3, which shows a full switchback stair against this same core).
